grammar ChemomerSmiles version "1.0.0" {
  ## The day-1 SMILES reader — atoms, bonds, branches, ring closures,
  ## bracket charges/isotopes/H-counts, aromatic markers — as a PARG
  ## text contract (chemomer#121). The reader builds the same
  ## graph::Structure the molfile walk produces; the oracle corpus's
  ## identity fixtures (all 1,543 carry SMILES + the recorded 1.07.5
  ## InChI) gate it byte-for-byte through the existing canonicalization.
  ##
  ## Phase 2 (carried — chemomer#128): tetrahedral @/@@ parity and
  ## directional / \ bonds ride into drawn geometry (the synthesis
  ## lays the parity ligands out and wedges the hand; the directional
  ## substituents lift to their drawn sides), so the /t and /b layers
  ## derive like a drawn molfile. %nn ring ids are captured. Still
  ## outside: dot-disconnected components (rejected — the corpus
  ## carries none) and SMILES writing (engine-side, algorithmic).
  ##
  ## Language notes: strict PEG, no repetition backtracking; the
  ## implicit bond between two aromatic atoms reads aromatic (the
  ## molfile's bond code 4), everything else implicit-single; the
  ## walk owns the ring-digit pairing and the branch stack.

  entry smiles: chain

  ## One connected component: an atom, then any number of
  ## continuations — a branch, a bonded atom, a bare atom (implicit
  ## bond), a bonded ring closure, or a bare ring closure.
  chain = ( atom 0*( part ) ) as chain

  part = ( branch / bonded_atom / bare_atom / bonded_ring / bare_ring )

  ## The branch point is the atom before the parens; the inner chain
  ## nests under `group` so the walk's depth-first order is the SMILES
  ## order.
  branch = ( "(" [ ( bond ) as b ] ( chain ) as group ")" ) as branch

  bonded_atom = ( ( bond ) as b ( atom ) )
  bare_atom = ( atom )

  bonded_ring = ( ( bond ) as b ( ringbond ) )
  bare_ring = ( ringbond )

  ## Ring-closure marker: one digit, or %nn for ids past 9. The walk
  ## pairs opens and closes by digit value; the optional bond symbol
  ## rides the bonded_* wrappers.
  ringbond = ( ( ( "%" 2( digit ) ) / ( digit ) ) as r )

  digit = ( %x30-39 )

  ## An atom: the bracket form or the organic subset. Either way the
  ## capture is one Hash carrying `sym` plus whatever bracket parts
  ## are present, so the walk reads one shape.
  atom = ( bracket / organic ) as a

  ## The organic subset: the aliphatic day-1 set plus the aromatic
  ## lowercase markers. Two-letter symbols first (the PEG order picks
  ## Cl over C).
  organic = ( ( ( "Cl" / "Br" ) / ( %x42 / %x43 / %x4E / %x4F / %x50 / %x53 / %x46 / %x49 ) / ( %x62 / %x63 / %x6E / %x6F / %x70 / %x73 ) ) as sym )

  ## The bracket form: isotope, element symbol (also the aromatic
  ## letters and `*`), chirality (captured, phase 2 for the walk),
  ## explicit H count, charge.
  bracket = ( "[" [ ( isotope ) as iso ] ( element ) as sym [ ( chirality ) as ch ] [ ( hcount ) as h ] [ ( charge ) as chg ] "]" )

  isotope = ( 1*3( digit ) )

  element = ( "Cl" / "Br" / "Se" / "Te" / "As" / ( %x41-5A ) [ ( %x61-7A ) ] / ( %x62 / %x63 / %x6E / %x6F / %x70 / %x73 / %x2A ) )

  chirality = ( "@" [ ( "@" ) / ( 2*3( %x41-5A / %x30-39 ) ) ] )

  hcount = ( "H" [ ( digit ) / ( %x3F ) ] )

  ## The charge: a sign with an optional 0-2 digit magnitude, or the
  ## repeated-sign spelling (`++` / `--`) where each repeat adds one
  ## (chemomer#126 — real-world writers spell ferric `[Fe++]`; the
  ## walk's parse_charge already folds the repeats).
  charge = ( ( ( "++" / "--" ) / ( ( "+" / "-" ) [ 0*2( digit ) ] ) ) )

  ## The bond symbols. `/` and `\` are directional (phase 2 semantics);
  ## `:` reads aromatic; absence means implicit (aromatic between two
  ## aromatic atoms, single otherwise).
  bond = ( "-" / "=" / "#" / "$" / ":" / "/" / "\\" / "~" )

  test smiles {
    accept "C"
    accept "CC"
    accept "C=C"
    accept "C#N"
    accept "ClCCBr"
    accept "c1ccccc1"
    accept "C1CCCCC1"
    accept "C1=CC=CC=C1"
    accept "CC(=O)O"
    accept "CC(C)Cc1ccccc1"
    accept "[NH4+]"
    accept "[OH-]"
    accept "[13CH4]"
    accept "[2H]C([2H])([2H])[2H]"
    accept "[Fe+2]"
    accept "[Fe++]"
    accept "[O--]"
    accept "[O-]C(=O)C"
    accept "n1ccccc1"
    accept "c1ccsc1"
    accept "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1"
    accept "OC(=O)[C@@H](N)Cc1ccccc1"
    accept "C1C"
    accept "[Xx]"
    reject "C."
    reject ".C"
    reject "C("
    reject "C%%1"
    reject "[CH4"
  }
}
